title: Docker compose logs and teardown must run from an EXIT trap in the artifacts example test
answers: GitHub Actions runner disk full after failed artifacts example run
docker images left behind when the artifacts example test exits early
why does docker compose down not run after a failed pull in test_mlflow_artifacts
cleanup skipped on failure in mlflow artifacts integration test
body:
Symptom: After a failed artifacts example run on CI, Docker images and containers are left on the runner, and the logs needed for debugging are missing.
Root cause: The old script set err=1 via `trap 'err=1' ERR`, then ran logs and down as plain lines. Any early exit (for example a failed pull) skipped both, so `--rmi all` never ran.
Fix pattern: Put `docker compose logs` and `docker compose down {rmi_option} --volumes --remove-orphans` in an `EXIT` trap in tests/tracking/test_mlflow_artifacts.py:test_mlflow_artifacts_example. The trap captures $? first, runs each step with `|| status=1`, and ends with `exit "$status"`, so the original failure code is kept and cleanup failures still fail the test.
Constraints: Cleanup must stay in the EXIT trap so it runs exactly once on every exit path. Do not add separate cleanup calls before `exit` in the script, which would bypass it or run it twice.
applies: Applies to the embedded shell script in tests/tracking/test_mlflow_artifacts.py:test_mlflow_artifacts_example and any similar compose-based example test.
says: Continuous integration build machine runs out of disk space when artifact examples fail.
Leftover containers and storage volumes clutter the test runner after an early abort.
Diagnostic logs are missing from the build output whenever an example job fails.
Ensure automated tests always clean up their background containers even when crashing unexpectedly.
search: In tests/tracking/test_mlflow_artifacts.py:test_mlflow_artifacts_example and similar compose-based example tests, docker compose logs and docker compose down with volume and orphan removal must run inside an EXIT trap. The trap captures $? first, executes each step with || status=1, and ends with exit "$status" to preserve failure codes without separate pre-exit cleanup calls.
